purpose: Inputs for lean/bound/compute.mjs: how much substitution the machine-checked Kimura fixation theorems allow in the flying-fish lineage over the time the fossil record gives it. Every value below names its source. Nothing here is measured by this thread; the Lean theorems take these as free parameters.

taxon.label: Exocoetidae (flying fishes)
taxon.darwin: On the Origin of Species (1859), chapter VI, Project Gutenberg text lines 5639-5642: flying-fish "might have been modified into perfectly winged animals" (organisms/darwin-origin/ch05-06/mentions.json).

durationMa.quantity: time elapsed since the family's oldest fossil occurrence, in millions of years

source.label: Paleobiology Database, data service 1.2, taxa/single for Exocoetidae with show=app: first appearance 56 to 48.07 Ma (Ypresian), 7 occurrences; oldest occurrence Rhamphexocoetus volans, Early Eocene (Monte Bolca).

durationMa.caveat: A fossil first appearance is a minimum age for the lineage; the crown group may be older, which would only raise the budget. The Ypresian occurrence is dated to an interval, so both ends are carried. Darwin's sentence looks forward from gliding to flight; the elapsed duration is the only measured span available, so the budget is what this lineage has already had, not what the transition would get.

sources.label: FishBase species summary for Hirundichthys affinis (fourwing flyingfish, Exocoetidae): "Generation time: 0.6 ( na - na) years. Estimated as median ln(3)/K based on 1 growth studies" and "max. reported age: 1.00 years (Ref. 6503)".
sources.reference: Campana, S.E., H.A. Oxenford and J.N. Smith (1993). Radiochemical determination of longevity in flyingfish Hirundichthys affinis using Th-228/Ra-228. Mar. Ecol. Prog. Ser. 100:211-219 (FishBase Ref. 6503).

sources.label: Chang, Yuan, Hoyle, Farley and Shiao (2022). Growth parameters and spawning season estimation of four important flyingfishes in the Kuroshio Current off Taiwan. Front. Mar. Sci. 8:747382. Sex-combined von Bertalanffy K between 3.534 and 4.350 per year for Cypselurus poecilopterus, Hirundichthys oxycephalus, Cheilopogon atrisignis and Cheilopogon unicolor; no age at maturity or generation time reported.

generationTimeYears.caveat: One species has a generation-time estimate, and it is a FishBase formula from one growth study. No family-wide value exists. The range 0.6 to 1.0 year follows the two FishBase numbers; a 2-year sensitivity case is reported separately because larger Cheilopogon species may live longer than Hirundichthys affinis, and no source was found that measures it.

mutationRatePerSitePerGeneration.quantity: germline mutation rate per site per generation

sources.label: Feng, Pettersson, Lamichhaney, Rubin, Rafati, Casini, Folkvord and Andersson (2017). Moderate nucleotide diversity in the Atlantic herring is associated with a low mutation rate. eLife 6:e23907. Pedigree estimate 2.0e-9 per site per generation, 95% CI 1.1e-9 to 2.9e-9.

Zhang, Reid, Sands, Fraimout, Schierup and Merila (2023). De novo mutation rates in sticklebacks. Mol. Biol. Evol. 40:msad192. Pedigree estimates 4.83e-9 and 4.29e-9 per base per generation in two marine populations of Pungitius pungitius.

mutationRatePerSitePerGeneration.caveat: No mutation-rate estimate exists for any Exocoetidae. Both sources are pedigree estimates in other teleost orders; the range is the lowest confidence bound to the highest point estimate among them.

genomeSites.quantity: sites per haploid genome used to convert per-site counts to per-genome counts

source.label: Xu, Zhao, You, Yang, Chen, Ruan, Gu, Xu, Bian and Shi (2021). Draft genome of the mirrorwing flyingfish (Hirundichthys speculiger). Front. Genet. 12:695700. "We obtained a 1.04-Gb genome assembly".

genomeSites.caveat: Assembly size, not the callable or functional fraction. The per-genome numbers are an upper envelope on sites, not a count of sites that matter for a wing.

populationSize.quantity: number of diploid individuals N; the chain has M = 2N gene copies

pointEstimates.what: effective population size from Bayesian demographic modelling of cytochrome b mtDNA (1106 bp, n = 266), described in the abstract as having increased ~150,000 years ago "to more than 1 billion individuals currently"
pointEstimates.source: Lewallen, Bohonak, Bonin, van Wijnen, Pitman and Lovejoy (2016). Population genetic structure of the tropical two-wing flyingfish (Exocoetus volitans). PLoS ONE 11:e0163198.
pointEstimates.caveat: mtDNA gives a female, maternally inherited effective size scaled by the paper's own generation-time and mutation-rate assumptions; it is the only published Ne for any Exocoetidae.

populationSize.caveat: Poorly constrained for the family. The ceiling is therefore reported as a function of N; the neutral budget and the floor do not depend on N (that is the content of the theorem).

selectionCoefficient.note: Undefined for the transition. The favored-chain theorem needs only that selection does not oppose the mutant (s >= 0); it gives no upper bound that depends on s.

fractionOfMutationsFavored.note: Undefined. The floor for adaptive substitutions is stated per favored mutation rate mu_f, which is at most the total rate mu and is not measured.

requiredSubstitutions.note: Undefined. 'Substitutions required for a wing' is not a defined quantity; no figure is invented, so the comparison the feasibility question needs cannot be made.
